close_reason: Replaced the misleading '# Cancellation' doc paragraph with an honest description: per-request cancellation is not supported in the current API, the spawned-task model prevents the obvious 'tokio::select! in your handler' workaround from working, and the recommended mitigations are (a) bound backend operations via tokio::time::timeout at the storage layer and (b) drain the dispatcher before shutdown rather than expecting handlers to respond to a server-wide signal. Filed JMAP-wlip.34 (labelled 'human') for the architectural decision on whether to add tokio_util / CancellationToken plumbing in a future API revision — that decision needs explicit input on workspace dep policy and API churn appetite.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:134-141. The doc comment under "# Cancellation" reads:

  If this future is dropped while a handler task is running (e.g., the
  HTTP connection closes), the spawned task runs to completion — tokio
  does not cancel tasks when their `JoinHandle` is dropped. The handler
  result is discarded. Callers that need strict cancellation should
  implement it at the handler level (e.g., `tokio::select!` with a
  shutdown signal).

The first sentence is correct and important. The "implement it at the handler level" advice is unworkable in practice for per-request cancellation:

1. The handler runs on `tokio::task::spawn` (lib.rs:177). The spawned task has no access to the outer (dispatch-future) context — no token, no shared mutex of "still alive" bits, nothing.
2. The handler signature is `JmapHandler<C>::call(&self, method: String, call_id: String, args: Value, caller: C) -> HandlerFuture`. No cancellation token.
3. The CallerCtx could carry a token (the consumer adds a `cancel: CancellationToken` field), but then EVERY handler must thread it through every `.await` site — every backend call, every database query, every blob fetch. The library provides no scaffolding.

What the doc says ("implement cancellation in your handler") only works for SERVER-WIDE shutdown signals (`tokio::select!` with a broadcast channel from main). It does not work for per-request cancellation triggered by HTTP client disconnect.

Production consequence: a JMAP server with a handler doing a long backend operation (e.g., Email/query over a 10M-mailbox account, a 30-second full-text search, a slow LDAP lookup for an Identity/get) cannot react to client disconnect. Every disconnect leaks resource consumption equal to the full backend cost. Adversarial clients can DoS by opening many requests and dropping them.

Fix shape: add an optional `cancel: tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` field on Dispatcher::dispatch (or on the CallerCtx, with the doc making the token-carrier pattern explicit). On dispatch-future drop, signal the token; the handler then races each .await against `cancel.cancelled()`. Document the wiring.

Alternative shape (cheaper, lower-power): skip the task::spawn entirely for handlers that are non-`UnwindSafe`-by-design and use catch_unwind from std::panic to keep panic isolation without the spawn. This makes the dispatch future itself responsible for cancellation propagation, no token plumbing needed — when the future drops, every running handler future drops with it. But losing tokio's panic-isolation guarantee is a hard call; tokio's spawn-and-await-the-JoinHandle gives clean panic-to-serverFail mapping. Mentioned for completeness; (1) is the recommended path.

Minimum fix (do not implement, just document): correct the doc to say "Per-request cancellation is not supported in the current API. Long-running backend operations should bound their own runtime via deadlines/timeouts at the backend layer. Server-wide shutdown via tokio::select! works only for the dispatcher loop, not for spawned handler tasks." Then file a follow-up bead for the real fix.
title: Dispatcher::dispatch documents tokio cancellation behaviour but the workable cancellation pattern requires a CancellationToken plumbing that doesn't exist
